newsitem.title: JAPAN: Minor Metals--Asia market quiet, cobalt soft.
newsitem.headline: Minor Metals--Asia market quiet, cobalt soft.

text.p: Minor metal markets were quiet in Asia as Chinese participants slowly returned from the Lunar New Year holidays, although traders in Japan said cobalt prices were slightly softer.
They said continued fighting between government and rebel forces in Zaire, a leading cobalt producer, was not yet lending much support to prices.
One trader linked the slight decline in part to manoeuvring ahead of a sale by the U.S. Defense Logistics Agency later this month, although the Japanese market was quiet.
"We always get weakness before a DLA sale," he said. He added that while the situation in Zaire was not at present affecting prices, traders were monitoring it closely.
In the antimony market, a Hong Kong-based trader said the market was watching supplies in Europe and he doubted the price would firm in the next week.

"Unsolicited offers for antimony are coming in at $2,300 per tonne, which means the price is negotiable. I think buying is possible at $2,280 per tonne and, if a seller wants cash badly, they could go as low as $2,250 per tonne."
One trader added that while some East Asian traders were reluctant to do business at current low prices, "customers are just buying hand-to-mouth, waiting for the prices to go lower".

Molybdenum was stable, although a Hong Kong source said there were a few big consumers in the market this week, apparently seeking a few hundred tonnes, and price direction would depend on the outcome of those deals.
A Japanese trader added that February was traditionally a slow month in Japan for molybdenum demand.
Bismuth remained on a weakening trend amid ample supplies. One trader said he bought a container last week at a low of $2.85 per pound.
"Many (in the market) overestimated demand for bismuth, and it"s now in a cyclical downturn, for example because the hunting season is over," he said. Bismuth is used in cartridges.
Tungsten business in China was still slow in the wake of the long Lunar New Year holiday, trading sources said.
One Hong Kong-based trading source said Chinese producers were offering material at above $4.00 per kg in an effort to compete in the European market with cheap Russian material.
Ferro tungsten was indicated in London last week at $5.50/6.00 per kg.
Traders gave the following current prices for minor metals, on a CIF basis at major Japanese ports, except for antimony, which is FOB Southern China:
